purpose: Allow citizens to challenge, correct, supplement or request review of an answer without allowing an unverified assertion to overwrite verified evidence, law or published snapshots.
core_principle: CITIZEN_FEEDBACK → CLASSIFY → PRESERVE → VERIFY → REVIEW → CORRECT OR CONFIRM → NEW SNAPSHOT IF REQUIRED
assertion_rules: Citizen statements remain assertions until independently established.
A citizen-provided document can be relevant evidence but is not automatically an official record.
A property-identity correction triggers property matching review before substantive conclusions are changed.
A date correction triggers temporal-scope review.
A legal challenge triggers authority/proposition review and does not itself establish a different legal rule.
A new document may change sufficiency only after identity, property and date validation.
Material correction to a published answer requires a new immutable snapshot rather than editing history.
public_response_rules: Explain what part of the answer was reviewed.
State whether the feedback changed the evidence, legal analysis, limitation or answer.
Do not expose internal chain-of-thought or private investigation metadata.
If unresolved, state what evidence or authority is still needed.
If materially revised, identify the new answer version and preserve the predecessor.
hard_stops: Never overwrite official evidence with citizen assertions.
Never silently alter a published answer.
Never suppress a material correction because it conflicts with an existing answer.
Never treat a user-uploaded document as official registration evidence without source validation.
Never convert disagreement alone into a new legal conclusion.
